Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA / Order Form - proposed capacity scale + implementation timing

Jordan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We’ve run the proposed orderform and there are a couple of items procurement / legal want surfaced as a formal change order rather than separate email threads:

- Move the implementation window from 60 days to 90 days for the initial phase and allow an 8-week ramp for integration.
- Add a temporary 20% price uplift for burst capacity for the first quarter after go-live (we understand this is a negotiation point).
- Clarify SLA language for inference latency credits when usage spikes exceed the burst pool.

Our contracts counsel (Simon) would like a single consolidated redline so they can route internally. Can you send the redline and an outline of the approval path? We will need: a short summary of business impact, which clauses change, and whether any of the changes require MSA-level signatory (vs order form only).

I attached a short note from our procurement team with the high-level ask. Happy to hop on a call — suggested times early next week.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morris
Director, Cloud Procurement
NovaCare Health

Team — forwarding NovaCare asks. Key asks from Elena: extend implementation window to 90 days, temporary 20% burst uplift for quarter 1, explicit SLA credit language for burst events.

Can legal confirm which of these are Order Form vs MSA? My read: implementation window and burst uplift are order-form changes; SLA language likely touches MSA behavior sections (Service Levels / Credits). Laura, can you take lead on redlines and indicate whether signatory escalation is required?

Karthik — can you give a quick commercial view on the 20% uplift and whether we can offer a phased reduction tied to usage? Also confirm proration approach if they shift start date.

Hannah — ops: can you validate whether the 90 day window plus an 8-week ramp is operationally reasonable for our dedicated onboarding schedule and whether we need an implementation exception clause for the early burst?

I’ve attached the initial proposed change order (simple docx with high-level asks) so legal can mark up. Will consolidate and send back to NovaCare by EOD next Thursday unless earlier is possible.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Redwood MSA / Order Form - proposed capacity scale + implementation timing

Jordan — quick summary from Legal after an initial pass:

- Implementation window: change is acceptable as an Order Form amendment; suggest we add a one-time "Implementation Exception" paragraph that documents the longer window and any milestone SLAs (to avoid reopening acceptance criteria in the MSA).
- Burst uplift (20%): can be handled on the Order Form fee schedule. Recommend adding a sunset clause tied to the first invoice quarter (i.e., ends at the last day of Q1 post-go-live) and an explicit metric for when the uplift drops (e.g., average sustained burst usage below threshold for 30 days).
- SLA / credits: the language in the MSA (Section 5) governs credits; any substantive change to credit calculation should be handled as an MSA amendment. If NovaCare wants a narrower credit carve-out limited to burst events, we can do it as an Order Form attachment that references the MSA calculations but does not alter core MSA definitions.

I’ve attached a marked-up Exhibit A and draft Order Form lines. Please review the edits in ExhibitA_markup.pdf and confirm: (1) whether we should route the MSA amendment to Exec Legal (they triage custom MSA edits), and (2) which signatory (VP Commercial or Head of GTM Ops) is appropriate for the Order Form uplift approval.

Attachments: ExhibitA_markup.pdf (pdf)

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Morris <elena.morris@novacare.tech>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Redwood MSA / Order Form - proposed capacity scale + implementation timing

Thanks Laura — commercial thoughts:

- 20% uplift for Q1 is acceptable for onboarding risk. Proposal: apply uplift only to burst units (not baseline committed units). After Q1, reduce uplift to 10% for an additional month if sustained usage remains above 120% of committed throughput, then revert to standard rates.
- Billing/proration: if NovaCare delays start beyond the agreed kickoff we should prorate the uplift and the implementation milestone invoices by the number of full weeks delayed; include an explicit early-termination credit if they cancel during ramp.
- SLA credits: we prefer to keep MSA intact. If NovaCare insists on Order Form language, limit it to clarifying how burst events are measured and to reference the MSA credit formula — do not change the calculation itself.

One question: Elena, can your team confirm whether the burst metric will be measured as a 5-minute tail percentile or a daily 95th percentile? That affects how often we'd credit.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Elena / Simon —

Thanks for the input and patience while we pulled together internal redlines. Attached is the consolidated package: Consolidated_MSARedlines_v1.docx (all edits tracked). Highlights and next steps:

1) Order Form changes (no MSA amendment required unless NovaCare requests formal change):
   - Implementation window extended to 90 days with an 8-week ramp schedule (Implementation Exception, Order Form Exhibit B).
   - Temporary 20% burst uplift applied to burst units for the first invoice quarter after go-live, sunset clause included; follow-on tapering to 10% based on sustained usage rule (commercial snapshot attached).
   - Proration language for delayed kickoff and an early-termination credit during ramp.

2) MSA-related language (no substantive amendment proposed):
   - We added an Order Form attachment that references MSA Section 5 credit calculations and defines measurement for burst events (we did not change the MSA credit formula). If NovaCare confirms they need a permanent change to credit calculations, we will route an MSA amendment via Exec Legal.

3) Routing & approvals:
   - Order Form redlines can be executed by the Head of GTM Ops for Order Form exceptions (please confirm on your side).
   - If NovaCare requires MSA amendment sign-off, indicate whether their legal seeks a full-exec signatory.

Attached: Consolidated_MSARedlines_v1.docx (docx)
Action items:
- Elena / Procurement: confirm your measurement preference (5-minute tail vs daily 95th) — that will lock the burst metric clause.
- NovaCare to confirm which internal signatory will execute the Order Form exception.
- If approved, we’ll prepare a DocuSign package and aim for signature within 5 business days after confirmation.
